# Model Overview ## Description: The NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr model is the LiLiCorr speculative decoding checkpoint for NVIDIA's Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B model family, which is a hybrid LatentMoE vision-language model designed for reasoning, chat, visual understanding, and agentic workflows. For details about the target model, see the [BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4) model cards. The NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr model is intended for LiLiCorr speculative decoding deployments tuned for DGX Spark and low-concurrency data center workflows. This model was built through our [ModelOpt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer) library which is a library of model optimization techniques including quantization, pruning, Neural Architecture Search (NAS), distillation, speculative decoding and sparsity to accelerate models. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ## License/Terms of Use: **GOVERNING DOWNLOAD TERMS:** Use of this model is governed by the [OpenMDW-1.1 model license](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/). ## Deployment Geography: Global ## Use Case: Developers deploying Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B for reasoning, chat, RAG, and agentic workflows that benefit from lower-latency speculative decoding on DGX Spark and data center GPUs. Load this draft checkpoint alongside the Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B target model to enable LiLiCorr-assisted serving. ## Release Date: Hugging Face - 10/15/2026 via [https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr) ## References - NVIDIA Model Optimizer: [https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer) - [NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16 reasoning model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16) - [NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 reasoning model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4) - [LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20530) ## Model Architecture: The LiLiCorr model architecture is as follows: **Architecture Type:** Dense GQA (Dense MLP + GQA Attention) **Network Architecture:** Dense FFN MLP, and GQA Attention layers; the LiLiCorr drafter's attention uses bidirectional grouped-query attention (GQA), with 32 query heads, 8 key-value heads, within the draft block and sliding-window attention over the most recent 8,192 context positions on all layers, with a grouped dynamic convolution around each attention and MLP sublayer. A separate two-layer LiLiCorr head correlates the drafter's top-8 candidates at each draft slot. **Number of Model Parameters:** 1.13B trained parameters (37M in the LiLiCorr head), plus a 0.54B NVFP4 copy of the target’s LM head. For details about the target model's architecture, see the [Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16), [Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4). ## Input: The inputs below describe the target-model serving interface. LiLiCorr drafts tokens using representations from the target model. **Input Type(s):** Text **Input Format(s):** Text: String **Input Parameters:** Text: One-Dimensional (1D) **Other Properties Related to Input:** The target model supports up to 1M tokens of context. The serving configuration below sets a 114,688-token limit. Supported languages include English, French, Spanish, Italian, German, Japanese, Hindi, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, and Chinese. ## Output: **Output Type(s):** Text **Output Format:** String **Output Parameters:** One-Dimensional (1D): Sequences **Other Properties Related to Output:** Input and generated output share the configured context window. The target model supports JSON output, reasoning output, and tool calling. Our AI models are designed and/or optimized to run on NVIDIA GPU-accelerated systems. By leveraging NVIDIA's hardware (e.g. GPU cores) and software frameworks (e.g., CUDA libraries), the model achieves faster training and inference times compared to CPU-only solutions. ## Software Integration: **Supported Runtime Engine(s):** - vLLM **Supported Hardware Microarchitecture Compatibility:** - NVIDIA Blackwell - including DGX Spark (GB10) - NVIDIA Hopper **Preferred Operating System(s):** - Linux The integration of foundation and fine-tuned models into AI systems requires additional testing using use-case-specific data to ensure safe and effective deployment. Following the V-model methodology, iterative testing and validation at both unit and system levels are essential to mitigate risks, meet technical and functional requirements, and ensure compliance with safety and ethical standards before deployment. ## Model Version(s): - v1.0 - LiLiCorr GA ## Training and Evaluation Datasets: ## Training Dataset: For more information about the underlying Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B model, please visit the model card - [Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16), [Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4). **Link**: [Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v2), [Nemotron-RL-Super-Training-Blends](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Super-Training-Blends), [Nemotron-Post-Training-v3](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-post-training-v3), [Nemotron-Instruction-Following-Chat-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Instruction-Following-Chat-v1), and [Nemotron-Science-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Science-v1). Prompts and conversation context from these datasets were used to synthesize training data. The final assistant response was regenerated with Nemotron-3.5-Super and used as the training target; earlier conversation turns and tool context were retained. **Data Modality:** Text **Text Training Data Size:** 22.6 Billion Tokens (4,096-token training windows), repeated for 3 epochs, followed by 35.6 Billion Tokens (8,192-token training windows), for 2.9 epochs (500K steps) **Data Collection Method by dataset:** Hybrid: Automated, manually-collected, Synthetic **Labeling Method by dataset:** Hybrid: Automated, manually-labelled, Synthetic **Properties:** The Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr model was trained exclusively on a post-training corpus that includes synthetic data for reasoning, math, code, science, tool use, agentic and software-engineering tasks, instruction following, chat, structured outputs, and multilingual tasks. Each final assistant response used as a training target was generated by Nemotron-3.5-Super at temperature 1.0: the model was first trained on responses from a Nemotron-3.5-Super post-training checkpoint, then finetuned on responses from the released checkpoint. Dataset disclosures are published in the linked Hugging Face datasets and the `nvidia/nemotron-post-training-v3` collection. For more information about the datasets used to train the target model, please see the [Public Summary of Training Content](https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/nemotron-3.5-super-vl/Nemotron_3.5_Super_VL_EU_Training_Content_Summary.pdf) ## Evaluation Dataset: The model is evaluated on the [SPEED-Bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) dataset for speculative decoding benchmarking. **Data Collection Method by dataset:** Hybrid: Automated, manually-collected, Synthetic **Labeling Method by dataset:** Hybrid: Automated, manually-labelled, Synthetic **Properties:** This corpus comprises a mix of high-quality standard benchmarks and test suites for LLMs. These benchmarks prompt the underlying model on a diverse set of tasks such as coding, math, writing, translation, etc., and speculative-decoding acceptance length is measured over the generated responses. ## Inference: **Acceleration Engine:** vLLM **Test Hardware:** NVIDIA Blackwell - DGX Spark (GB10) ## LiLiCorr Speculative Decoding Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B supports two speculative decoding paths, including native MTP and LiLiCorr for DGX Spark and low-concurrency data center workflows. This release is the LiLiCorr speculative decoding checkpoint intended to be paired with the Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B target model. LiLiCorr is designed to improve accepted length while preserving the latency benefits of block drafting on compact Blackwell systems such as DGX Spark. ## Usage To serve the checkpoint with [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), refer to the LiLiCorr recipes in the [NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B Model Card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4#quick-start) ## Evaluation Acceptance rate on [SPEED-Bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) with draft length 7: | Category | Acceptance Length - T=0 | Acceptance Length - T=1 | | --- | --: | --: | | coding | **5.65** | **5.29** | | humanities | **3.94** | **3.51** | | math | **4.93** | **4.56** | | multilingual | **5.53** | **5.04** | | qa | **4.37** | **4.03** | | rag | **5.69** | **5.33** | | reasoning | **4.87** | **4.54** | | roleplay | **3.78** | **3.46** | | stem | **4.11** | **3.69** | | summarization | **5.37** | **4.96** | | writing | **3.92** | **3.58** | | **Overall Average** | **4.74** | **4.36** | > Baseline: [Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4) > Benchmarked on SPEED-Bench Qualitative split (880 prompts) with a draft length of 7, concurrency 64, and a mean over 3 seeds. `temperature=1.0` uses `top_p=0.95`. ## Model Limitations: The target model may generate inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise undesirable responses, even when prompts are benign. It may reflect biases or content artifacts present in its training data, and output quality can vary by domain, language, reasoning depth, and context length. Developers should add application-specific safeguards and evaluate the system in the intended deployment environment before production use. ## Ethical Considerations NVIDIA believes Trustworthy AI is a shared responsibility and we have established policies and practices to enable development for a wide array of AI applications. # d1-3B

d1-3B is a 3B parameter **decision model** built on [LFM2.5-VL-3B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-3B).
You give it a state (text, JSON, images, or a mix) and a set of questions. It returns calibrated,
typed answers in **one forward pass with zero output tokens**.

- **Best decision model under 10B on the Decision Index 0.2.1**: 48.57, ahead of every 4B and 9B model
and of Decider 35B-A3B (47.11).
- **Multimodal**: images and text in the same state. It scores 74.1 on 11 public image benchmarks
(LFM2.5-VL-3B: 73.9).
- **Fast**: 8 ms a decision on an NVIDIA RTX 4090, 9 ms on an AMD MI325X, 30 ms on an Apple M5 Pro.

Find more information about open d1 in our [blog post](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/open-d1).

![image](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/61b8e2ba285851687028d395/r2H7UlZ_m48SYAhZWIHiu.png)

> 💻 **Demos**: Try d1-3B in a Hugging Face space without any setup:
> [**Open d1 Arcade**](https://huggingface.co/spaces/LiquidAI/system-one-arcade): Collection of 10 demos using d1-3B

## 🗒️ Model Details

| Model | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [LFM2.5-VL-3B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-3B) | 3.1B | General-purpose vision-language model (base) |
| **[d1-3B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B)** | 3.1B | Post-trained for single-pass, calibrated decisions |

d1-3B is a multimodal decision model with the following features:

- **Total parameters**: 3.12B
- **Vision encoder**: SigLIP2 NaFlex shape-optimized 400M
- **Context length**: 32,768 tokens
- **Vocabulary size**: 128,000

We recommend d1-3B wherever a pipeline needs a yes/no, a pick from named options, or a rating:
routing and triage, moderation, intent and topic classification, extraction checks, reranking, LLM-as-a-judge
scoring, agent guardrails, and visual inspection. It is not a chat model and does not write text.

## 🏃 How to use

Install the dependencies (requires `transformers>=5.14`):

```bash
pip install "transformers>=5.14" torch torchvision pillow
```

The model ships its own code, so load it with `trust_remote_code=True`:

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel
from transformers.image_utils import load_image

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
dtype = torch.float32 if device == "cpu" else torch.bfloat16
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/d1-3B", trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype).to(device)

# Text: several named questions over one state, answered in one pass
questions = {
    "refund": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is the customer asking for a refund?",
    },
    "team": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "Which team should handle this?",
        "criteria": {
            "billing": "Charges, refunds, invoices",
            "technical": "App or site faults",
            "fraud": "Suspected unauthorised use",
        },
    },
    "urgency": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "How urgent is this?",
        "criteria": ["Can wait", "Today", "Blocking the customer now"],
    },
}
print(model.system_one("I was charged twice this month, please refund one of them.", questions))

# Image: the photo is the whole state
image = load_image("http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg")  # two cats on a sofa
cats = {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "How many cats are there?",
    "criteria": {"one": "One", "two": "Two", "more": "Three or more"},
}
print(model.system_one(None, {"cats": cats}, images=[image]))

# Batch: many requests, packed together with no padding
tickets = ["Where is my parcel? It was due Monday.", "The app crashes when I open settings."]
print(model.system_one_batch([(t, {"team": questions["team"]}) for t in tickets]))
```

| call |  |
| --- | --- |
| `system_one(state, questions, images=None)` | Named questions over one state, in one pass. The state and its images are read once for all questions. |
| `system_one_batch([(state, questions[, images]), ...])` | Many requests, packed with no padding. |

A state is a string, any JSON value, or `None` when the images are the whole state.

### Questions and answers

Questions follow the Decision Index schema: `type`, `instructions`, and `criteria`.

| `type` | `criteria` | answer fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `noul`: yes or no | optional: `{"true": "...", "false": "..."}` to define each side | `noul`: P(yes) |
| `choice`: one of named options | `{name: description}` | `choice`, `confidence`, `probabilities` |
| `score`: 2 to 10 ordered levels | a list of level descriptions, lowest first | `score` (the expected level), `confidence`, `probabilities`, `legend` |

Each call returns `{"answers": {name: answer}, "usage": {"input_tokens": n, "output_tokens": 0}}`.

## ⚡ Speed

Warm calls, one request at a time: a single question, three questions over one state, a 3.4k-token
state and a 384 px image. The last column is throughput with 64 states packed into one pass.

### Edge Inference

We measure latency on an Apple M5 Pro and, in collaboration with NVIDIA, on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor,
a Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB and a Jetson Orin Nano.

|  | one question | 3 questions, one pass | 3.4k-token state | 384 px image | 64 states, packed |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| Apple M5 Pro (`mps`) | 30 ms | 41 ms | 640 ms | 62 ms | 78 / s |
| NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor | 16 ms | 20 ms | 220 ms | 35 ms | 262 / s |
| NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB | 26 ms | 35 ms | 560 ms | 83 ms | 110 / s |
| NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano | 50 ms | 73 ms | 1640 ms | 202 ms | 38 / s |

### GPU Inference

We measure latency on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 and an AMD MI325X, in bf16, median of 20 runs.

|  | one question | 3 questions, one pass | 3.4k-token state | 384 px image | 64 states, packed |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 | 8 ms | 21 ms | 102 ms | 17 ms | 475 / s |
| AMD MI325X | 9 ms | 14 ms | 44 ms | 18 ms | 1,106 / s |

On NVIDIA GPUs, `model.compile(mode="reduce-overhead")` runs single questions as CUDA graphs (the RTX 4090
row uses it). Without it, a single question takes 16 ms. The first call with a new shape pays for kernel
selection or compilation, so warm up the shapes you serve.

# Deepthought: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL plus d1

## Finding

Plausible candidate for replacing Qwen Flash Next, not validated for shared residency. No weights downloaded, model loaded, service stopped, or production configuration changed during this investigation. Qwen remained healthy at the last check.

Deepthought has approximately 121 GiB unified RAM and 2.3 TiB free disk. With Qwen running, approximately 19 GiB RAM is available. Do not start the candidate beside Qwen.

## Verified artifacts

Repository metadata queried from Deepthought with Hugging Face's SDK, without loading custom code:

| Repository | Revision | Safetensors bytes | GiB |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 | 1334cab80531ccc1845c38a526f4ddfa1e43b849 | 75010188240 | 69.859 |
| nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr | 7c7221aeb4cb3139307aa457f7dce11a8fb6ceb2 | 1317952596 | 1.227 |
| LiquidAI/d1-3B | da1fe36a861f24690f27f622dca1d8688503d113 | 6247065504 | 5.818 |

Combined weights: approximately 76.904 GiB. This is file size, NOT measured resident or peak memory. KV and Mamba caches, vision workspaces, CUDA graphs, allocators, loading copies, and the OS need additional memory.

NVIDIA publishes a recipe specifically for this Nemotron checkpoint on one DGX Spark. It recommends LiLiCorr, seven speculative tokens, one concurrent sequence, FlashInfer Mamba, float16 SSM cache with stochastic rounding, qwen3_coder tool parsing, and nemotron_v3 reasoning parsing. Do not copy the GB200 or older Nemotron 3.0 recipe.

The documented Docker tag vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 returned not found. The documented exact nightly exists:

- Tag: vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3f1bcfd82bb2e93fcd364fc7a5491718453a77e2
- Verified linux/arm64 image: sha256:fd33bec1578f312a01547cc6b9691a5154c3e8bcfb76d2b35acb657bfc4eee8f
- Image config: CUDA 13.0.2; vLLM source commit matches the tag.
- Host driver: 580.178.04. No driver upgrade is proposed; actual kernels remain untested.

The d1 model card documents native CUDA BF16 inference via Transformers >=5.14 and model.system_one. The repository's existing serving recipe is CPU-only. It must be adapted and tested in an isolated ARM64/CUDA environment; its x86 CPU dependency lock must not be reused as a GPU lock. Do not replace native decision probabilities with generated chat JSON or carry over CPU-int8 thresholds.

## Proposed trial, not yet authorized or executed

1. Stage pinned artifacts in a separate directory. Review checkpoint custom code before execution. Preserve Qwen's image, weights, service, and client configuration.
2. Confirm a maintenance window and stop Qwen before any candidate GPU loading.
3. Measure d1 alone: cold load, warm Choice/Yes-No/Score validity, memory peaks, and representative journal-state latency. Stop it before loading Nemotron alone.
4. Measure Nemotron alone with one sequence and an explicit initial 32K context ceiling. Bound cache allocation; a shorter context alone does not stop vLLM filling its configured memory budget. Begin with text, then test one image and a validated tool-call round trip. Do not enable large video requests initially.
5. Review separate peak measurements and reserve host headroom before approving a controlled shared-residency test. Measure d1 tail latency during Nemotron prefill and decode, startup/warm-up peaks, and worst permitted image requests. Process/container memory limits do not account for every GPU-driver allocation; monitor host MemAvailable too.
6. Only after the pair passes, install persistent services with a startup plan that excludes Qwen. Then connect Marvin's mrmr journal source in shadow mode over a private authenticated connection. No automatic remediation or agent effects.

Success means valid native decisions and usable decision latency while the worker is busy, not merely two healthy endpoints. Throughput, image correctness, tool correctness, shared-memory stability, and model quality have not been measured. Qwen rollback requires stopping all candidate GPU processes first; its existing cold load takes roughly 11–15 minutes.

"""Offline HTTP boundary checks; no Torch, weights, credentials, or network service."""

import copy
import http.client
import json
import threading
import unittest

from serve import DecisionServer, MAX_BODY, model_id


class ServingTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_http_contract_and_rejection(self):
        # Own and join the server thread even on assertion failure. The fake
        # only supplies inference; serialization/auth/validation use real HTTP.
        calls = []
        fail = False
        identity = model_id()
        token = "synthetic-test-token-not-a-secret-1234"

        def decide(state, questions):
            if fail:
                raise RuntimeError("private model state must not escape")
            calls.append((state, questions))
            return {
                "answers": {
                    "category": {"type": "choice", "choice": "incident", "confidence": 0.9,
                                 "probabilities": {"incident": 0.9, "noise": 0.1}},
                    "action": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.8},
                    "severity": {"type": "score", "score": 0.8, "confidence": 0.8,
                                 "probabilities": {"0": 0.2, "1": 0.8},
                                 "legend": {"0": "Low", "1": "High"}},
                },
                "usage": {"input_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 0},
            }

        server = DecisionServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), decide, token, identity)
        worker = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
        worker.start()

        def request(body, auth=token, path="/v1/systemone", method="POST", extra=None):
            conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(*server.server_address, timeout=3)
            try:
                headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + auth, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
                headers.update(extra or {})
                conn.request(method, path, body, headers)
                response = conn.getresponse()
                return response.status, json.loads(response.read())
            finally:
                conn.close()

        valid = {
            "model": identity,
            "state": {"data": {"message": "Synthetic incident", "id": 9007199254740993}},
            "questions": {
                "category": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Classify", "criteria": {"incident": "Broken", "noise": "Routine"}},
                "action": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Act?", "criteria": {"true": "Yes", "false": "No"}},
                "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "Severity?", "criteria": ["Low", "High"]},
            },
        }
        try:
            status, result = request(json.dumps(valid))
            self.assertEqual(status, 200)
            self.assertEqual(result["model"], identity)
            self.assertEqual(result["usage"]["output_tokens"], 0)
            self.assertEqual(calls[0][0]["data"]["id"], 9007199254740993)
            self.assertEqual(set(result["answers"]), set(valid["questions"]))
            self.assertEqual(request(None, path="/health", method="GET")[0], 200)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", auth="wrong")[0], 401)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", path="/chat/completions")[0], 404)
            self.assertEqual(request("x" * (MAX_BODY + 1))[0], 413)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", extra={"Content-Type": "text/plain"})[0], 415)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", extra={"Transfer-Encoding": "chunked"})[0], 400)
            for raw in ["{", "[]", "{}", '{"state": 1, "state": 2}',
                        json.dumps(valid).replace('"Synthetic incident"', "NaN"),
                        json.dumps(valid).replace('"Synthetic incident"', "1e999")]:
                self.assertEqual(request(raw)[0], 400)
            for patch in [
                {"model": model_id(True)}, {"images": ["http://never-fetch.invalid"]},
                {"questions": {}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "unknown", "instructions": "?"}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "noul", "instructions": ""}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "?", "criteria": {"true": "Yes"}}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "score", "instructions": "?", "criteria": ["One"]}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "?", "criteria": {"a.b": "A", "b": "B"}}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "?", "criteria": {"a": 1, "b": "B"}}}},
            ]:
                value = copy.deepcopy(valid)
                value.update(patch)
                self.assertEqual(request(json.dumps(value))[0], 400)
            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1, "invalid requests must never reach inference")
            fail = True
            status, result = request(json.dumps(valid))
            self.assertEqual(status, 500)
            self.assertNotIn("private", json.dumps(result))
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            worker.join(timeout=3)
            server.server_close()
            self.assertFalse(worker.is_alive())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded synthetic timings through the same decider used by the HTTP server.

Not a quality evaluation. Never substitutes for labeled real events. Load and
warm timings are separate, and Linux peak RSS includes model loading/conversion.
"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import resource
import statistics
import time

from serve import load_decider, model_id


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--int8", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    started = time.perf_counter()
    decide = load_decider(args.checkpoint.resolve(), 4, args.int8)
    print(json.dumps({"model": model_id(args.int8), "load_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}), flush=True)
    questions = {
        "category": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which category best describes this system service event?", "criteria": {
            "incident": "A service is broken, unavailable, repeatedly failing, or losing data now.",
            "noise": "Routine startup, shutdown, retry, or warning chatter needing no attention.",
            "FYI": "Useful operational information that is neither an incident nor routine noise.",
        }},
        "requires_action": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the operator genuinely need to take action?"},
        "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How severe is the operational impact?", "criteria": ["No impact", "Degraded with workaround", "Unavailable or data at risk"]},
    }
    short = "The service has failed repeatedly and is unavailable."
    for name, state, qs in [
        ("one", short, {"category": questions["category"]}),
        ("three", short, questions),
        ("longer", "Routine heartbeat: the service is healthy. " * 20 + "Now the disk is full and all writes fail.", questions),
    ]:
        times = []
        for _ in range(4):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            result = decide(state, qs)
            times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)
        assert result["usage"]["output_tokens"] == 0
        assert set(result["answers"]) == set(qs)
        print(json.dumps({
            "workload": name, "cold_seconds": times[0],
            "warm_median_seconds": statistics.median(times[1:]), "warm_seconds": times[1:],
            "usage": result["usage"], "answers": result["answers"],
            "peak_rss_kib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss,
        }, allow_nan=False), flush=True)
    # Ensure an over-limit request fails before spending inference, not after
    # the runtime's HTTP timeout. This checks the real pinned tokenizer path.
    try:
        decide("heartbeat " * 2000, questions)
    except ValueError:
        print('{"over_limit_rejected": true}', flush=True)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("token ceiling was not enforced")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from typing import Any

class D1Model(Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration):

    def engine(self) -> SystemOne:
        from transformers import AutoTokenizer

        return SystemOne(model=self.eval(), tokenizer=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(self.name_or_path))

    def system_one(self, state: Any, questions: Mapping[str, Any], images: Sequence | None = None) -> dict:

        `{"answers": {name: answer}, "usage": {"input_tokens": n, "output_tokens": 0}}`."""
        return self.engine.system_one(state, questions, images)

"""One-pass typed decisions on a causal LFM backbone.

The model sees the state and the question once, and the answer is read off the
logits at the answer slot. Nothing is decoded, so a schema violation is
impossible and `tokens generated per decision` is zero.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Any, Sequence

import torch

from .api import SystemOneApi
from .lfm2_vl import Lfm2ForCausalLM, Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration
from .prompt import (
    DEFAULT_MODEL,
    DEFAULT_STATE_STYLE,
    DEFAULT_SYSTEM,
    IM_START,
    Question,
    default_lead,
    prefix_text,
    readout,
    render,
    suffix_text,
)

# Every picture is bounded at this many pixels before the processor.
VISION_MAX_PIXELS = 1024 * 1024


# LFM2 models run on the hybrid stack (`hybrid.py`); any other model type through transformers as it is.
MODELS = {
    "lfm2_vl": Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration,
    "lfm2": Lfm2ForCausalLM,
}


def load_backbone(model_id: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    """The checkpoint and its tokenizer, with SDPA attention."""
    from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText, AutoTokenizer, PretrainedConfig

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tok.pad_token_id is None:
        tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    kind = PretrainedConfig.get_config_dict(model_id)[0].get("model_type")
    cls = MODELS.get(kind, AutoModelForImageTextToText)
    return cls.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=dtype, attn_implementation="sdpa"), tok


def cap_pixels(image, max_pixels: int = VISION_MAX_PIXELS):
    """A picture downscaled to at most `max_pixels`, bicubic."""
    image = image.convert("RGB") if hasattr(image, "convert") else image
    w, h = image.size
    if w * h <= max_pixels:
        return image
    try:
        from PIL import Image
    except ImportError as e:  # optional for text
        raise ImportError("resizing a picture needs Pillow") from e

    scale = math.sqrt(max_pixels / (w * h))
    return image.resize((max(1, int(w * scale)), max(1, int(h * scale))), Image.Resampling.BICUBIC)


class SystemOne(SystemOneApi):
    """State in, calibrated distribution out, one forward pass."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model_id: str = DEFAULT_MODEL,
        device: str | None = None,
        calibration=None,
        lead: str | None = None,
        state_style: str = DEFAULT_STATE_STYLE,
        system: str = DEFAULT_SYSTEM,
        option_style: str = "desc",
        compile: bool = False,
        token_budget: int = 65536,
        model=None,
        tokenizer=None,
    ):
        """`model` and `tokenizer`, when given, are a backbone already loaded (`D1Model` passes itself);
        it stays on its device unless `device` says otherwise."""
        if model is None:
            model, tokenizer = load_backbone(model_id)
        else:
            model_id, device = model.config._name_or_path, device or next(model.parameters()).device
        self.model, self.tokenizer = model, tokenizer
        self.model_id = model_id
        if lead is None:
            lead = default_lead(self.model.config.model_type)
        self.device = torch.device(device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
        self.model.to(self.device).eval()
        bos = getattr(self.tokenizer, "bos_token", None)
        self.bos = bos if isinstance(bos, str) else ""
        self.calibration = calibration
        self.lead = lead
        self.state_style = state_style
        self.system = system
        self.option_style = option_style
        self.token_budget = token_budget
        self.processor = None
        # CUDA graphs for single questions on NVIDIA, where eager time is mostly kernel launches.
        if compile and torch.version.hip:
            raise ValueError("compile=True needs CUDA: on ROCm the CUDA graphs fault after a few dozen calls")
        self._one_pass = (torch.compile(self.model.forward, mode="reduce-overhead")
                          if compile else self.model)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- prompt

    def render(self, state: Any, q: Question) -> str:
        return render(
            self.tokenizer, state, q, self.bos, self.lead, self.state_style,
            self.system, self.option_style,
        )

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- forward

    def _logz_ids(self, rows: list[list[int]]) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
        """Log-softmax at the answer slot, one row per token list, in one pass.

        The rows are one tree (`hybrid.py`): their common start is its trunk and
        is read once; the rest of each row is a branch, packed with no padding.
        Mathematically each row alone; in bf16 the kernels differ by batch shape.
        """
        if len(rows) == 1:  # nothing to share: a plain chain is faster than a tree of one
            row = self._one_pass(input_ids=torch.tensor(rows, device=self.device), logits_to_keep=1).logits[0, -1]
            return [row.float() - torch.logsumexp(row.float(), dim=-1)]
        shared = 0  # every row keeps at least its last token
        while shared < min(map(len, rows)) - 1 and len({r[shared] for r in rows}) == 1:
            shared += 1
        return self._tree_logz(rows[0][:shared], [r[shared:] for r in rows])

    def _tree_logz(self, trunk: list[int], rows: list[list[int]], **vision) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
        """`trunk` then each of `rows`, read at each row's end."""
        packed = torch.tensor([t for r in rows for t in r], device=self.device)
        lengths = torch.tensor([len(r) for r in rows], device=self.device)
        trunk = torch.tensor([trunk], dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
        logits = self.model.answer(trunk, packed, lengths, **vision).float()
        return list(logits - torch.logsumexp(logits, dim=-1, keepdim=True))

    def plan_batches(self, texts: Sequence[str], token_budget: int | None = None) -> list[list[int]]:
        """Consecutive batches of at most `token_budget` tokens: rows are packed,
        so a batch costs its real tokens."""
        return self._plan([len(self.tokenizer.encode(t, add_special_tokens=False)) for t in texts], token_budget)

    def _plan(self, lengths: Sequence[int], token_budget: int | None = None) -> list[list[int]]:
        if not lengths:
            return []
        budget = token_budget or self.token_budget
        out: list[list[int]] = [[]]
        used = 0
        for i, n in enumerate(lengths):
            if out[-1] and used + n > budget:
                out.append([])
                used = 0
            out[-1].append(i)
            used += n
        return out

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- readout

    def _readout(self, q: Question, logz: torch.Tensor) -> list[float]:
        return readout(self.tokenizer, q, logz, self.calibration)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- api

    @torch.inference_mode()
    def run(self, requests: Sequence[tuple[Any, list[Question], Sequence]]) -> list[tuple[list[list[float]], int]]:
        """Each `(state, questions, images)` request's probabilities and the tokens it read. Requests of one
        question and no pictures are packed together, one tree per token budget; any other request is its
        own pass, its state (and pictures) the trunk and its questions the branches."""
        out: list = [None] * len(requests)
        single = [i for i, (_, qs, images) in enumerate(requests) if len(qs) == 1 and not images]
        rows = [self.tokenizer.encode(self.render(requests[i][0], requests[i][1][0]), add_special_tokens=False)
                for i in single]
        for chunk in self._plan([len(r) for r in rows]):
            for j, z in zip(chunk, self._logz_ids([rows[j] for j in chunk])):
                out[single[j]] = ([self._readout(requests[single[j]][1][0], z)], len(rows[j]))
        for i, (state, qs, images) in enumerate(requests):
            if out[i] is None:
                out[i] = self._request(state, qs, images)
        return out

    def _request(self, state: Any, qs: list[Question], images: Sequence) -> tuple[list[list[float]], int]:
        pics = [cap_pixels(im) for im in images]
        prefix = prefix_text(self.tokenizer, state, self.bos, self.state_style, self.system,
                             self._image_markup(len(pics)) if pics else "")
        suffixes = [suffix_text(self.tokenizer, q, self.lead, self.option_style) for q in qs]
        vision: dict = {}
        if not pics:
            trunk = self.tokenizer.encode(prefix, add_special_tokens=False)
        elif len(qs) == 1:  # the whole prompt in one plain pass
            inputs = self._image_inputs(prefix + suffixes[0], pics)
            row = self._one_pass(**inputs, logits_to_keep=1).logits[0, -1].float()
            return [self._readout(qs[0], row - torch.logsumexp(row, dim=-1))], int(inputs["input_ids"].shape[1])
        else:
            vision = self._image_inputs(prefix, pics)
            trunk = vision.pop("input_ids")[0].tolist()
            vision.pop("attention_mask", None)
        branches = [self.tokenizer.encode(s, add_special_tokens=False) for s in suffixes]
        probs: list[list[float]] = []
        for chunk in self._plan([len(b) for b in branches]):
            zs = self._tree_logz(trunk, [branches[j] for j in chunk], **vision)
            probs += [self._readout(qs[j], z) for j, z in zip(chunk, zs)]
        return probs, len(trunk) + sum(map(len, branches))

    def tokens(self, state: Any, questions: Sequence[Question]) -> int:
        """The longest prompt one of `questions` makes over a text state: its state's tokens and its own."""
        prefix = prefix_text(self.tokenizer, state, self.bos, self.state_style, self.system)
        return len(self.tokenizer.encode(prefix, add_special_tokens=False)) + max(
            len(self.tokenizer.encode(suffix_text(self.tokenizer, q, self.lead, self.option_style),
                                      add_special_tokens=False)) for q in questions)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- vision

    def _image_markup(self, n: int) -> str:
        """What the chat template writes for `n` images at the head of a user turn (`<image>` each on LFM2-VL)."""
        if self.processor is None:
            self.processor = self._load_processor()
        msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": [*([{"type": "image"}] * n), {"type": "text", "text": "\x00"}]}]
        text = self.processor.apply_chat_template(msgs, add_generation_prompt=False, tokenize=False)
        head = f"{IM_START}user\n"
        return text[text.index(head) + len(head):text.index("\x00")]

    def _load_processor(self):
        from transformers import AutoProcessor

        return AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(self.model.config._name_or_path, trust_remote_code=True)

    def _image_inputs(self, text: str, images: Sequence) -> dict:
        """Token ids and pixel inputs for one prompt holding `images`; the prompt carries its own BOS."""
        inputs = self.processor(text=[text], images=[list(images)], return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False)
        if "pixel_attention_mask" in inputs:
            # LFM2-VL's processor pads every image to 1024 patches and the tower
            # masks the padding out; cutting it gives the same answer for up to
            # half the work.
            n = int(inputs["pixel_attention_mask"].sum(1).max())
            inputs["pixel_values"] = inputs["pixel_values"][:, :n]
            inputs["pixel_attention_mask"] = inputs["pixel_attention_mask"][:, :n]
        return {k: (v.to(self.device) if hasattr(v, "to") else v) for k, v in inputs.items()}

"""The System One API: named questions over a state in, typed answers out.

    model.system_one(state, {"refund": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this a refund request?"}})
    # {"answers": {"refund": {"type": "noul", "noul": p}}, "usage": {"input_tokens": n, "output_tokens": 0}}

A state is a string, any JSON value, or None with pictures alone. A question is a dict in the Decision
Index's schema (`type`, `instructions`, `criteria`) or one of `prompt`'s classes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from typing import Any

from .prompt import Choice, Noul, Question, as_question


def answer(q: Question, probs: Sequence[float]) -> dict:
    """A noul's P(yes); a choice's pick and its probabilities; a score's expected level."""
    if isinstance(q, Noul):
        return {"type": "noul", "noul": probs[0]}
    best = max(range(len(probs)), key=probs.__getitem__)
    if isinstance(q, Choice):
        names = list(q.criteria)
        return {"type": "choice", "choice": names[best], "confidence": probs[best],
                "probabilities": dict(zip(names, probs))}
    return {"type": "score", "score": sum(i * p for i, p in enumerate(probs)), "confidence": probs[best],
            "probabilities": {str(i): p for i, p in enumerate(probs)},
            "legend": {str(i): text for i, text in enumerate(q.criteria)}}


class SystemOneApi:
    """`system_one` and `system_one_batch`, and the plain probabilities under them, over a model's
    `run(requests)`: each `(state, questions, images)` request's probabilities (in its questions' order)
    and the tokens it read."""

    def run(self, requests: Sequence[tuple[Any, list[Question], Sequence]]) -> list[tuple[list[list[float]], int]]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def probabilities(self, state: Any, questions: Sequence, images: Sequence | None = None) -> list[list[float]]:
        """Each question's distribution over its options (`yes`, `no` for a noul), in one pass."""
        return self.run([(state, [as_question(q) for q in questions], images or ())])[0][0]

    def probabilities_batch(self, requests: Sequence[tuple]) -> list[list[list[float]]]:
        """`probabilities` for many `(state, questions[, images])` requests, packed as `system_one_batch`."""
        reqs = [(r[0], [as_question(q) for q in r[1]], (r[2] if len(r) > 2 else None) or ()) for r in requests]
        return [probs for probs, _ in self.run(reqs)]

    def system_one(self, state: Any, questions: Mapping[str, Any], images: Sequence | None = None) -> dict:
        """Named questions over one state, and its pictures if any, in one forward pass."""
        return self.system_one_batch([(state, questions, images)])[0]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Opt-in real-model integration check. Owns all processes and uses only synthetic data.

Run under the resource-limited scope in README.md. No service is installed, no
source starts, and the temporary database/configuration are removed on exit.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import yaml

from serve import model_id


def stop(process):
    if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
        process.terminate()
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=15)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            process.kill()
            process.wait()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--int8", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    recipe = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    binary = str(args.binary.resolve())
    env = dict(os.environ, MRMR_D1_API_KEY=secrets.token_hex(32))
    # Never stop an existing listener to make a test work. Both processes will
    # also fail binding if another process wins the small check/start race.
    for port in (8091, 4242):
        with socket.socket() as sock:
            # Match HTTPServer/Go listener reuse: TIME_WAIT from our previous
            # check is not a live listener and must not block a second run.
            sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
            sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
    # Ignore HTTP proxy environment variables: synthetic local traffic and the
    # bearer token must never be sent through a configured external proxy.
    http = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))

    def request(url, body=None, auth=False):
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if auth:
            headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + env["MRMR_D1_API_KEY"]
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None, headers=headers)
        with http.open(req, timeout=180) as response:
            return json.load(response)

    def ready(process, port, model=False):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 90
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if process.poll() is not None:
                raise RuntimeError("owned process exited before ready")
            try:
                if model:
                    health = request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health", auth=True)
                    assert health["model"] == model_id(args.int8)
                else:
                    with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=1):
                        pass
                return
            except (OSError, urllib.error.URLError):
                time.sleep(0.2)
        raise RuntimeError("owned process did not become ready")

    model_process = runtime_process = None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="mrmr-d1-smoke-") as tmp:
        # Logs contain only synthetic events. Keep them private and temporary;
        # never copy live journal data into this verification harness.
        os.chmod(tmp, 0o700)
        with open(Path(tmp) / "process.log", "w") as log:
            try:
                command = [sys.executable, str(recipe / "serve.py"), "--checkpoint", str(args.checkpoint.resolve())]
                if args.int8:
                    command.append("--int8")
                model_process = subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log)
                ready(model_process, 8091, model=True)
                cfg = yaml.safe_load((recipe / "mrmr.example.yaml").read_text())
                cfg["models"]["d1"]["model"] = model_id(args.int8)
                cfg["db"]["path"] = str(Path(tmp) / "smoke.db")
                # Force only the synthetic smoke through a shadow notification.
                # This checks the successful pipeline, not classification quality.
                cfg["policy"] = []
                cfg["default"] = {"notify": {"via": "stdout"}, "shadow": True}
                config = str(Path(tmp) / "mrmr.yaml")
                Path(config).write_text(yaml.safe_dump(cfg))

                def start_runtime():
                    process = subprocess.Popen([binary, "run", "-config", config], env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log)
                    # The caller owns cleanup even if readiness fails.
                    return process

                runtime_process = start_runtime()
                ready(runtime_process, 4242)
                event = {
                    "type": "setup.test", "source": "d1-smoke", "subject": "synthetic-service",
                    "data": {"message": "Synthetic incident: the fictional service is unavailable and all writes fail."},
                    "metadata": {"source_event_id": "synthetic-1"},
                }
                started = time.perf_counter()
                result = request("http://127.0.0.1:4242/api/events", event)
                elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
                assert result["decision"]["status"] == "ok", "model response was not accepted"
                assert result["decision"]["model"] == model_id(args.int8)
                assert result["outcome"] == "notify"

                def inspect():
                    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output([binary, "inspect", result["event_id"], "-config", config], env=env, stderr=log))

                stored = inspect()
                assert len(stored["decisions"]) == len(stored["executions"]) == 1
                assert stored["executions"][0]["status"] == "shadow"
                assert stored["trace"]
                assert request("http://127.0.0.1:4242/api/events", event)["duplicate"]
                stop(runtime_process)
                runtime_process = start_runtime()
                ready(runtime_process, 4242)
                assert request("http://127.0.0.1:4242/api/events", event)["duplicate"]
                assert len(inspect()["decisions"]) == 1
                print(json.dumps({"model": model_id(args.int8), "pipeline_seconds": elapsed,
                                  "decision": "ok", "execution": "shadow", "persisted_trace": True,
                                  "dedup_before_and_after_restart": True}), flush=True)
            finally:
                stop(runtime_process)
                stop(model_process)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Pin device selection without importing Torch or allocating GPU memory."""
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from serve import load_decider, model_id, private_host


class DeviceTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_identity_and_listen_boundary(self):
        self.assertTrue(model_id().endswith(":cpu-fp32"))
        self.assertTrue(model_id(True).endswith(":cpu-int8-channel"))
        self.assertTrue(model_id(device="cuda").endswith(":cuda-bf16"))
        for device, int8 in [("cuda", True), ("auto", False)]:
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                model_id(int8, device)
        for host in ["127.0.0.1", "100.99.177.33"]:
            self.assertEqual(private_host(host), host)
        for host in ["0.0.0.0", "8.8.8.8", "192.168.1.2", "100.128.0.1", "::1", "localhost"]:
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                private_host(host)

    def test_cuda_loader_and_token_bound(self):
        torch, auto = MagicMock(), MagicMock()
        model = auto.from_pretrained.return_value.eval.return_value.to.return_value
        model.engine.tokens.return_value = 12
        prompt = SimpleNamespace(as_question=lambda q: q)
        # The loader owns device/dtype selection; native model math is tested on hardware.
        with patch.dict(sys.modules, {"torch": torch, "transformers": SimpleNamespace(AutoModel=auto)}), \
                patch("serve.importlib.import_module", return_value=prompt):
            torch.cuda.is_available.return_value = True
            decide = load_decider(Path("/synthetic-checkpoint"), 4, device="cuda")
            self.assertEqual(auto.from_pretrained.call_args.kwargs["dtype"], torch.bfloat16)
            self.assertTrue(auto.from_pretrained.call_args.kwargs["local_files_only"])
            auto.from_pretrained.return_value.eval.return_value.to.assert_called_once_with("cuda")
            decide("synthetic", {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Relevant?"}})
            model.system_one.assert_called_once()
            model.engine.tokens.return_value = 1025
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                decide("synthetic", {"q": {}})
            self.assertEqual(model.system_one.call_count, 1)
            auto.reset_mock()
            torch.cuda.is_available.return_value = False
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                load_decider(Path("/synthetic-checkpoint"), 4, device="cuda")
            auto.from_pretrained.assert_not_called()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def system_one_batch(self, requests: Sequence[tuple]) -> list[dict]:
        """Many `(state, questions)` or `(state, questions, images)` requests. Single-question requests
        are packed together with no padding; a request with several questions reads its state once."""
        named = [(r[0], {n: as_question(q) for n, q in r[1].items()}, (r[2] if len(r) > 2 else None) or ())
                 for r in requests]
        done = self.run([(state, list(qs.values()), images) for state, qs, images in named])
        return [{"answers": {n: answer(q, p) for (n, q), p in zip(qs.items(), probs)},
                 "usage": {"input_tokens": read, "output_tokens": 0}}
                for (_, qs, _), (probs, read) in zip(named, done)]

"""The pieces every LFM hybrid is made of, and the one shape that makes many
questions cost about one forward.

A model runs a batch of right-padded chains `(B, T)`, or a tree: a trunk of P
tokens (the state) and N branches (the questions) that each continue it, packed
back to back on one axis with no padding, `[trunk | branch 0 | branch 1 | ...]`.
Everything that works token by token (norms, projections, the MLP) runs once
over the packed axis. A convolution continues each branch from the trunk's last
inputs. Attention runs by parts: the trunk causally, every branch token over the
trunk in one flash call that reads the trunk's keys once for all questions
(under sliding attention, one fp32 product over the trunk's last window-1 keys),
each branch over its own tokens in one varlen flash call, the two merged by
their log-sum-exp. Nothing is cached, copied or padded.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from transformers.modeling_layers import GradientCheckpointingLayer
from transformers.modeling_outputs import BaseModelOutputWithPast

Tensor = torch.Tensor


class Tree:
    """A trunk of `p` tokens and branches of `lengths` tokens, packed on one axis."""

    def __init__(self, p: int, lengths: Tensor):
        self.p, self.n = p, len(lengths)
        self.cu = F.pad(lengths.cumsum(0), (1, 0)).int()  # where each branch starts, past the trunk
        self.longest = int(lengths.max())
        self.branch = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(self.n, device=lengths.device), lengths)
        self.offset = torch.arange(len(self.branch), device=lengths.device) - self.cu[self.branch]
        # a branch starts where the trunk ends
        self.positions = torch.cat((torch.arange(p, device=lengths.device), p + self.offset))
        self.leaves = p + self.cu[1:].long() - 1  # each branch's last token
        self._conv = {}

    def conv_order(self, keep: int) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
        """Gather and keep indices that run one causal conv over all branches,
        each led by the trunk's last `keep` inputs. Indices are into the whole
        input left-padded by `keep` zeros."""
        if keep not in self._conv:
            p, total, dev = self.p, len(self.branch), self.branch.device
            slot = torch.arange(total, device=dev) + keep * (self.branch + 1)
            order = torch.empty(total + self.n * keep, dtype=torch.long, device=dev)
            order[slot] = keep + p + torch.arange(total, device=dev)
            lead = (self.cu[:-1] + keep * torch.arange(self.n, device=dev))[:, None]
            order[lead + torch.arange(keep, device=dev)] = p + torch.arange(keep, device=dev)
            self._conv[keep] = order, slot - keep
        return self._conv[keep]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# norms and rotary
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class RMSNorm(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, eps: float):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(dim))
        self.eps = eps

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        x32 = x.float()
        return (x32 * torch.rsqrt(x32.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + self.eps)).type_as(x) * self.weight


def cos_sin(angles: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    angles = torch.cat((angles, angles), dim=-1)
    return angles.cos(), angles.sin()


def rotate(x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Half-split RoPE in fp32; `cos`/`sin` broadcast over the head axis."""
    x32 = x.float()
    a, b = x32.chunk(2, dim=-1)
    return (x32 * cos + torch.cat((-b, a), dim=-1) * sin).type_as(x)


def rope(x: Tensor, pos: Tensor, theta: float, rotated: int) -> Tensor:
    """RoPE over `(B, T, H, D)` at positions `pos` `(T,)`, pairs past `rotated` left as they are."""
    dim = x.shape[-1]
    inv = 1.0 / theta ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2, device=x.device).float() / dim)
    inv[rotated:] = 0.0
    cos, sin = cos_sin(pos.float()[:, None] * inv)
    return rotate(x, cos[:, None], sin[:, None])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# causal convolution
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def causal_conv(x: Tensor, weight: Tensor, tree: Tree | None) -> Tensor:
    """Depthwise causal conv over `(B, C, T)`; a tree's branches continue its trunk."""
    keep = weight.shape[-1] - 1
    padded = F.pad(x, (keep, 0))
    if tree is None:
        return F.conv1d(padded, weight, groups=x.shape[1])
    order, kept = tree.conv_order(keep)
    branches = F.conv1d(padded[..., order], weight, groups=x.shape[1])[..., kept]
    if tree.p == 0:
        return branches
    return torch.cat((F.conv1d(padded[..., : keep + tree.p], weight, groups=x.shape[1]), branches), dim=-1)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# attention, `(B, H, T, D)`
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


# queries per explicit product off the flash kernels, which bounds its fp32 scores
CHUNK = 1024


def _fused(q: Tensor) -> bool:
    """Whether the flash kernels take these queries: a GPU in half precision, ROCm or CUDA from Ampere on."""
    if not q.is_cuda or q.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
        return False
    return bool(torch.version.hip) or torch.cuda.get_device_capability(q.device)[0] >= 8


def _explicit(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, allowed: Tensor | None, scale: float) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Attention with its log-sum-exp, in fp32, for small key sets. GQA by broadcast."""
    groups = q.shape[1] // k.shape[1]
    k, v = k.repeat_interleave(groups, dim=1).float(), v.repeat_interleave(groups, dim=1).float()
    scores = (q.float() @ k.transpose(-1, -2)) * scale
    if allowed is not None:
        scores = scores.masked_fill(~allowed, float("-inf"))
    return torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1).nan_to_num() @ v, torch.logsumexp(scores, dim=-1)


def _cat(parts: list[tuple[Tensor, Tensor]]) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    return torch.cat([o for o, _ in parts], dim=2), torch.cat([lse for _, lse in parts], dim=2)


def _over_trunk(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, scale: float) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Every branch token over all of the trunk, with its log-sum-exp. Each KV
    head's query group is folded into the query axis, so the trunk's keys are
    read once and never repeated."""
    batch, heads, length, dim = q.shape
    kv = k.shape[1]
    if not _fused(q):
        return _cat([_explicit(part, k, v, None, scale) for part in q.split(CHUNK, dim=2)])
    folded = q.reshape(batch, kv, heads // kv * length, dim)
    out, lse = torch.ops.aten._scaled_dot_product_flash_attention(folded, k, v, 0.0, False, False, scale=scale)[:2]
    return out.reshape(batch, heads, length, dim).float(), lse.reshape(batch, heads, length)


def _own(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, tree: Tree, window: int | None, scale: float) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Each branch over its own tokens, causally (within `window`), with its log-sum-exp."""
    if not _fused(q) and len(tree.branch) <= CHUNK:  # small enough for one masked product
        same, off = tree.branch[:, None] == tree.branch[None], tree.offset
        allowed = same & (off[None] <= off[:, None])
        if window is not None:
            allowed &= off[None] > off[:, None] - window
        return _explicit(q, k, v, allowed, scale)
    if not _fused(q):  # branch by branch: memory grows with the longest question, not with the batch
        parts = []
        for a, b in zip(tree.cu[:-1].tolist(), tree.cu[1:].tolist()):
            off = torch.arange(b - a, device=q.device)
            allowed = off[None] <= off[:, None]
            if window is not None:
                allowed &= off[None] > off[:, None] - window
            parts.append(_explicit(q[:, :, a:b], k[:, :, a:b], v[:, :, a:b], allowed, scale))
        return _cat(parts)
    local = {} if window is None else {"window_size_left": window - 1, "window_size_right": 0}
    out, lse = torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward(
        *(t[0].transpose(0, 1) for t in (q, k, v)), tree.cu, tree.cu, tree.longest, tree.longest,
        0.0, True, False, scale=scale, **local)[:2]
    return out.transpose(0, 1)[None].float(), lse[None]


def _merge(a: tuple[Tensor, Tensor], b: tuple[Tensor, Tensor]) -> Tensor:
    (oa, la), (ob, lb) = a, b
    m = torch.maximum(la, lb)
    wa, wb = (la - m).exp(), (lb - m).exp()
    return (oa * wa[..., None] + ob * wb[..., None]) / (wa + wb)[..., None]


def _windowed(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, window: int, scale: float) -> Tensor:
    """Causal attention within `window`, as local blocks: each block of `window`
    queries sees its own block and the one before it."""
    batch, heads, length, dim = q.shape
    blocks = -(-length // window)

    def split(t: Tensor) -> Tensor:  # (B, H, T, D) -> (B, blocks, H, window, D)
        t = F.pad(t, (0, 0, 0, blocks * window - length))
        return t.reshape(batch, t.shape[1], blocks, window, dim).transpose(1, 2)

    def with_previous(t: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        return torch.cat((F.pad(t, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :-1], t), dim=3)

    qb, kb, vb = split(q), with_previous(split(k)), with_previous(split(v))
    qpos = torch.arange(window, device=q.device)[:, None] + window
    kpos = torch.arange(2 * window, device=q.device)[None, :]
    allowed = (kpos <= qpos) & (kpos > qpos - window)
    first = allowed & (kpos >= window)  # block 0 has no block before it
    mask = torch.stack([first] + [allowed] * (blocks - 1))[:, None].repeat(batch, 1, 1, 1)
    out = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(qb.flatten(0, 1), kb.flatten(0, 1), vb.flatten(0, 1),
                                         attn_mask=mask, scale=scale, enable_gqa=True)
    out = out.reshape(batch, blocks, heads, window, dim).transpose(1, 2)
    return out.reshape(batch, heads, blocks * window, dim)[:, :, :length]


def causal_attention(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, window: int | None, scale: float) -> Tensor:
    """Right-padded chains: causal, within `window` if set."""
    if window is None or q.shape[2] <= window:
        return F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True, scale=scale, enable_gqa=True)
    return _windowed(q, k, v, window, scale)


def attention(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, tree: Tree | None, window: int | None, scale: float) -> Tensor:
    """Chains, or a tree: the trunk causally, each branch over the trunk and over
    its own tokens."""
    if tree is None:
        return causal_attention(q, k, v, window, scale)
    p = tree.p
    qb = q[:, :, p:]
    mine = _own(qb, k[:, :, p:], v[:, :, p:], tree, window, scale)
    if p == 0:
        return mine[0].to(q.dtype)
    trunk = causal_attention(q[:, :, :p], k[:, :, :p], v[:, :, :p], window, scale)
    if window is None:
        seen = _over_trunk(qb, k[:, :, :p], v[:, :, :p], scale)
    else:  # only the trunk's last window-1 keys are in reach of a branch
        tail = min(p, window - 1)
        allowed = torch.arange(p - tail, p, device=q.device)[None] > tree.positions[p:, None] - window
        seen = _explicit(qb, k[:, :, p - tail:p], v[:, :, p - tail:p], allowed, scale)
    return torch.cat((trunk, _merge(seen, mine).to(q.dtype)), dim=2)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the stack
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class DecoderLayer(GradientCheckpointingLayer):
    """Norm, operator (`conv` or `self_attn`), residual; norm, MLP, residual.
    `sandwich` adds a norm on each branch's output."""

    def __init__(self, kind: str, operator: nn.Module, mlp: nn.Module, dim: int, eps: float, sandwich: bool):
        super().__init__()
        self.operator_name = "conv" if kind == "conv" else "self_attn"
        setattr(self, self.operator_name, operator)
        self.feed_forward = mlp
        self.operator_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps)
        self.ffn_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps)
        self.post_operator_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps) if sandwich else nn.Identity()
        self.post_ffn_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps) if sandwich else nn.Identity()

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, pos: Tensor, tree: Tree | None = None) -> Tensor:
        h = x + self.post_operator_norm(getattr(self, self.operator_name)(self.operator_norm(x), pos, tree))
        return h + self.post_ffn_norm(self.feed_forward(self.ffn_norm(h)))


class LanguageModel(nn.Module):
    """Embedding, the hybrid stack and the final norm, called like HF's text models.

    Rows are right-padded, so the causal operators never let a pad reach a real
    token and there is no attention mask to apply.
    """

    def __init__(self, cfg, operator: Callable[[str], nn.Module], mlp: Callable[[], nn.Module],
                 eps: float, sandwich: bool = False):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed_tokens = nn.Embedding(cfg.vocab_size, cfg.hidden_size)
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
            DecoderLayer(kind, operator(kind), mlp(), cfg.hidden_size, eps, sandwich) for kind in cfg.layer_types)
        self.embedding_norm = RMSNorm(cfg.hidden_size, eps)  # the final norm, despite its name

    def get_input_embeddings(self) -> nn.Embedding:
        return self.embed_tokens

    def run(self, h: Tensor, tree: Tree | None = None) -> Tensor:
        pos = tree.positions if tree is not None else torch.arange(h.shape[1], device=h.device)
        for layer in self.layers:
            h = layer(h, pos, tree)
        return self.embedding_norm(h)

    def forward(self, input_ids=None, inputs_embeds=None, **_) -> BaseModelOutputWithPast:
        h = self.embed_tokens(input_ids) if inputs_embeds is None else inputs_embeds
        return BaseModelOutputWithPast(last_hidden_state=self.run(h))

    def answer(self, trunk: Tensor, questions: Tensor, lengths: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """Final hidden states at the last token of every question, in one pass.
        `trunk` `(1, P, d)` embeddings; `questions` the ids of all questions back
        to back, `(sum(lengths),)`."""
        tree = Tree(trunk.shape[1], lengths)
        h = self.run(torch.cat((trunk, self.embed_tokens(questions)[None]), dim=1), tree)
        return h[0, tree.leaves]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stop only an owned trial container if host memory headroom becomes unsafe."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time


def available_gib(text):
    values = dict(line.split(":", 1) for line in text.splitlines())
    return int(values["MemAvailable"].split()[0]) / 1024**2


assert available_gib("MemAvailable: 12582912 kB\nMemFree: 1 kB") == 12
name = sys.argv[1]
assert name in {"nemotron35-trial", "d1-benchmark", "d1-smoke", "d1-serve"}
seen, low = False, 0
with open(Path("results") / (name + "-memory.jsonl"), "a") as output:
    # RuntimeMaxSec and the wrapper own shutdown; this is not a detached daemon.
    for _ in range(3600):
        result = subprocess.run(["docker", "inspect", "-f", "{{.State.Running}}", name],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
        running = result.returncode == 0 and result.stdout.strip() == "true"
        if seen and not running:
            break
        seen = seen or running
        memory = available_gib(Path("/proc/meminfo").read_text())
        output.write(json.dumps({"time": time.time(), "available_gib": memory, "running": running}) + "\n")
        output.flush()
        low = low + 1 if memory < 12 else 0
        if running and (memory < 8 or low >= 3):
            print("Memory guard stopped " + name, flush=True)
            subprocess.run(["docker", "stop", "-t", "10", name], check=True, timeout=30)
            sys.exit(1)
        time.sleep(2)
